version.description: The version being agreed to — the one the person was shown.

oneOf.description: Present when the account is counting down to deletion.

history.description: Everything before, newest first, warnings included.

email.description: Administrators only, as are the next four.

setupPending.description: Made by staff and not yet set up by the person (administrators only).

chapterIds.description: Narrow what they may change to these chapters. Omitted, the whole work.

name.description: What to call them, since an address is a poor way to recognise a friend.

entries.description: Answers started, drafts included: a prompt with any cannot be deleted.

days.description: Tomorrow and the two weeks after it, then today and the two weeks before.

queue.description: The queue, in the order it will be used.

warning.description: Set when fewer than seven are queued.

chapterId.description: Required for a chapter-scoped question, ignored otherwise.

daysLeft.description:
Days until the account is deleted, for an appeal on a closing
restriction. The purge waits for the decision.

nextBefore.description: Pass as `before` for the page after this one; unset at the first day.

after.description: The scene's text after the selection. Only the start of it is sent on.

before.description:
The scene's text before the selection, or before the cursor. Only the
end of it is sent on.

instruction.description: What the writer wants: how to rewrite, or what to ask.

selection.description: The selected passage. Needed to rewrite or proofread; optional to ask.

AssistTask.description: What the writer asked the assistant to do.

actorId.description: Who did it. Kept after their account is gone.

AuthorCard.description: Author cards attached to comments so the clients need no second round trip.

BlockChangeKind.description: One paragraph's fate between two versions.

beforeIndex.description: Index of this paragraph in the earlier version, when it was in it.

changes.description: Word-level detail, for a modified paragraph.

counts.description: Totals, for the author only — see the note on `list_reactions`.

oneOf.description: What the viewer themselves marked, if anything.

quote.description:
The opening of the paragraph, so the author's list reads as prose
rather than as coordinates. Empty if the block has since gone.

userId.description:
Who to shut out. An id rather than an address: this is somebody who has
already turned up.

source.description:
The one source they all share: bulk dismissal is for a flood from the
same place, not for sweeping the queue.

authorId.description: Only this author's proposals, when set.

stale.description:
Proposals whose text has moved on too far to place automatically. They
stay pending: refusing is safer than guessing where they meant.

commentIds.description: Named ids win outright; without them the filters below choose.

options.description:
Settings shared by every file; the per-format blocks (`pdf`, `epub`,
`html`) apply to their own format only.

days.description:
The new length in days (3, 7 or 30), or `null` for permanent. Left out,
the length stays.

role.description:
`chapter`, `front`, `back` or `part`. Front and back matter are not
numbered and are included or left out of an export on their own; a
part is a divider before its chapters and is not numbered as one.

appealOpen.description: Waiting on an appeal: the deletion happens only once it is decided.

chapterIds.description:
The chapters they may change, when they were handed only some. Absent
means the whole work.

email.description:
The address it went to. Shown to owners only: the people on a book do
not need each other's addresses to work on it.

oneOf.description: Who they are, once they have an account and have opened the work.

moderationState.description:
`visible`, `held` or `removed`: what site moderation has done with it,
apart from the author's own delete.

authorScore.description:
How useful this reviewer's notes have proved elsewhere — votes plus the
notes authors marked resolved. Shown beside the name so a reader with a
record of being right is legible as one.

replies.description:
Threads nest arbitrarily deep, which makes this type self-referential.
Schema generation has to be told to stop, or it recurses until the stack
gives out.

CommentsMode.description: What to do with the writer's own comments.

aboutAuthor.description: Append the writer's *About the author* text as back matter.

backMatter.description: `None` takes the preset's default: off for manuscript, on for book.

oneOf.description: For endnotes: at the end of each chapter, or of the book.

quotePassage.description:
`None`: off for footnotes, on for endnotes, where the note is far from
its passage.

toc.description:
`None` takes the format's own default: on for EPUB, whose navigation
document is required, and off elsewhere.

payload.description:
The replacement text for `insert` and `replace`, or the mark name for
`format`. Ignored for `delete`.

title.description:
Left out or empty, it is untitled and shown as "Chapter 2" for where it
falls, until the writer names it.

oneOf.description: Present for highlight-to-comment; absent for a general note.

templateId.description:
A sketch template (`GET /api/notebook/templates`) to start from: its fields
arrive empty, ready to fill in.

maxReviewers.description: How many people may comment. Omitted, there is no cap.

scopeRefId.description: Chapter or scene id when `scope` is narrower than the whole work.

spoilerSafe.description:
Withhold notes on scenes a reader has not reached. Omitted, it follows
the work: on for a serial, off for anything else.

scope.description: `work` asks it once; `chapter` asks it of every chapter on offer.

title.description:
Left out or empty, it is untitled and shown as "Scene 2" for where it
falls, until the writer names it.

quote.description: The passage it is about, when it was written against one.

oneOf.description:
`work` (the default), `chapter` or `scene`. A smaller snapshot is for
checkpointing one chapter before rewriting it, without implying
anything about the rest of the book.

scopeRefId.description: The chapter or scene being frozen, when narrower than the whole work.

templateId.description: Omit for a single empty chapter and scene.

oneOf.description: Unset on a removed critique kept for its replies.

canRemove.description: The caller may delete it: their own, or any on their own answer.

moderated.description:
`removed` (by a moderator; shown as a placeholder) or `held` (awaiting
review; only its writer and staff see it).

day.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, the Pacific prompt day; `None` while it waits in the queue.

restoreContent.description: On `overturned`: bring back what was removed alongside it.

code.description: From the authenticator, when two-factor sign-in is on.

deleteSharedWorks.description:
Required when a work being deleted has co-authors on it, after they
have been told which.

confirmName.description: The account's display name, typed to confirm.

deleteSharedWorks.description: Go ahead although other people are working on books this account owns.

skipExport.description:
Don't email the person a copy of their data first. Needs the reason
above to say why (a spam account, say).

from.description: What each side is called — a version's label, or "Working draft".

oneOf.description: The version behind each side, absent when it is the working copy.

text.description:
"Yesterday: 4 critiques and 2 replies on your answer to '…'. Today's
prompt is open."

code.description: From the authenticator, or a recovery code.

DocNode.description:
The document shape, declared for the generated schema.

The server stores and forwards scene bodies as opaque `serde_json::Value` —
the editor owns the schema, and the server has no reason to validate beyond
`validate()` above. But "opaque" would generate as `unknown` in the clients,
which is exactly the kind of untyped hole this contract exists to close, so
the fields carrying a document declare this type instead.

emailVerified.description: Email can only be turned on for a confirmed address.

opensAtLocal.description:
When today's prompt opens (and so when it closes), as `HH:MM` in
`email_timezone`, for the note beside the time.

moderated.description: `held` (awaiting review) or `removed`, on the writer's own answer.

fields.description: The sketch, in order. Empty for an entry that is just a name and notes.

sceneIds.description: Scenes this entry appears in, in reading order.

coverPage.description: Also a cover page in the spine, not just the cover image.

splitChapters.description: One XHTML file per chapter (the default) or the whole book in one.

details.description: Present when the client is expected to act on it — see a scene save conflict.

requestId.description: The request's id, as in its `x-request-id` header and its log lines.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
The shape every failure comes back as. Declared for the generated schema so
clients can type their error handling instead of guessing.

profile.description: The profile these options came from, for the export history.

ExternalConfig.description:
What `/admin/external` saves, in `moderation_settings` under `external`.
The two secrets are stored sealed (see `secrets`) and never sent back.

banScope.description:
The scope a temporary ban or suspension from the platform is given:
`discussion` (the default) or `site`.

removeAs.description: What the platform's *remove* does here: `hold` (the default) or `block`.

apiKey.description: Set only when given; stored encrypted and never shown again.

apiKeySet.description: The secrets are never sent back; only whether they are set.

backlog.description: Checks waiting for the platform to come back.

webhookUrl.description: Where the platform should send its webhooks.

assistant.description: Whether this server has the writing assistant.

summaries.description: Whether this server can write summaries at all.

summaryProvider.description: Who writes them, for the consent screen.

FolioStyle.description: How the page number is written.

canDownload.description:
Whether the file can be made again: it came from a frozen version, and
did not depend on comments, which can change.

ImportProfileRequest.description:
A profile from a `.json` file someone saved, perhaps from an older version
or another instance. Unlike saving from the dialog, the options are taken
leniently: what no longer exists falls back to its default and is listed
in `notes`, rather than refusing the whole file.

link.description: A path in the web app.

oneOf.description: The newest unread summary, pinned above the items.

invited.description:
The addresses as understood: trimmed, lowercased, each once. The same
whether or not they were mailed, for the reason at the top.

remainingToday.description: How many more addresses the writer can invite today.

accepted.description: Whether that reader has opened it yet.

Issue.description:
A thing worth knowing before the file goes out. `code` is stable: the web
app keys on it, so a message can be reworded without breaking anything.

message.description: Says what to do next, not just what went wrong.

key.description: What the run is for: the day, for a daily job.

externalBacklog.description: Public posts waiting for the moderation platform to come back.

externalUnapplied.description: Events from the platform that were stored and not applied.

runs.description: The most recent runs, newest first.

timezone.description:
The writer's timezone (IANA), from their browser. Sets the default
time for the email, which stays off until they turn it on.

byFormat.description: The latest of each format, which the dialog opens with.

oneOf.description: The most recent export of any format, which "Export again" repeats.

ticket.description: Single use, good for thirty seconds: `GET /api/live?ticket=…`.

origin.description: `scheduled deletion` for a purge; `external` for the platform.

code.description:
The six digits from an authenticator, or a recovery code, for an
account with two-factor sign-in on. Asked for with a
`two_factor_required` refusal when it is missing.

days.description: How long it works, 1 to 90 days.

baseHash.description: Both scenes' hashes, so a merge cannot silently swallow someone's edit.

with.description: The scene to absorb. It must sit in the same chapter.

MetadataOverrides.description:
Export-time replacements for the work's own metadata. They apply to this
export only: a pen name for an EPUB, while the project keeps the writer's.

coverWarning.description: Set when the cover is smaller than e-readers like.

closing.description: Ends in the account being deleted.

day.description: Pin it to this future day instead of queueing it.

changes.description: Word-level detail for an edited paragraph.

now.description: What that paragraph says now, when it still says anything.

NoteStatus.description: What became of the text a note was attached to.

position.description:
Where it sits among the entries of its kind, as the writer arranged
them; 0 first. Absent from an entry cached before it existed.

templateId.description: The sketch template it was started from, if any.

oneOf.description:
The caller's standing on the work, so a client can offer only what the
server will accept. Sent on every outline; optional so an outline a
client cached before collaboration existed still decodes.

Where the caller was when they last had the book open, to put them
back there. Absent the first time, or once that scene is gone.

endingSoon.description: Restrictions ending in the next 24 hours.

waitingOnAppeal.description: Closing accounts whose deletion is waiting on an open appeal.

PdfOptions.description: Page setup for PDF. Book-layout PDF reads these; manuscript PDF is fixed.

insideMarginIn.description:
The inside (binding) edge, mirrored on facing pages. `None` is a little
more than the margin, for the gutter.

marginIn.description: Inches; `None` is 1. The top, bottom and outside edges.

pageNumbers.description: Page numbers on the pages of the book (not on chapter openings).

filename.description:
The name the download will have, so the dialog can show it as the
template is typed.

ok.description: False when any issue is an error. Warnings never block.

publications.description:
What this author has on offer that the viewer could open — the same
rule the feed applies, so a profile never lists a locked door.

reviews.description: Other people's work this person has given notes on, newest first.

viewerFollows.description: Whether the person asking follows this author. Always false signed out.

id.description: `builtin:…` for the ones that ship with the app.

notes.description:
What had to change to make a saved profile work today: a font that was
withdrawn, a setting that was renamed.

sceneId.description: The scene the reader is looking at.

editedAt.description: The last change made after submitting.

moderationState.description: `visible`, `held` or `removed`, apart from the author's own state.

submittedAt.description: The first submission. Never moved by an edit or a resubmission.

content.description: The answer, as a ProseMirror document.

oneOf.description: The last project made from it, if it still exists.

myState.description: The caller's own answer: `none`, or the entry's state.

opensAt.description: When it opened and when it closes.

submissions.description: How many have been submitted, late ones included.

maxReviewers.description:
How many people may comment. Beta readers are scarce, and twenty
overlapping opinions are worse than five considered ones.

spoilerSafe.description:
Withhold notes on scenes a reader has not reached yet. Defaulted on for
a serial, where not knowing yet is the whole point of reading one.

authorReviewsGiven.description:
Other people's publications this author has left notes on — what lifts
their work in the needs-readers queue.

excerpt.description:
First lines of the published slice, for the feed. Filled in after the
database round trip because it comes off disk — always sent, even when
empty, so clients do not have to treat it as optional.

readerCount.description: Distinct people who have opened it or left a note, the author excepted.

snippet.description:
Words around what a search matched, when this card came from one;
matched words sit between U+0002 and U+0003.

baseHash.description:
The `contentHash` the client believes it is editing on top of. When it
no longer matches, someone else — another tab, another device, a queued
offline save — has written in the meantime, and this save is refused
rather than silently overwriting their work.

Omitted only when there is nothing to protect: a scene the client has
not read yet. To resolve a conflict deliberately, re-send with the hash
the 409 reported, which says "I have seen their version and still mean
this".

createRevision.description: Autosaves pass `false`; explicit saves and idle-flushes pass `true`.

localDay.description:
The writer's local date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, so this save counts toward the
right day. Omitted, it is not recorded against any day at all: skipping
a tally is better than crediting the wrong one.

context.description: Where it sits: the publication, the prompt, what it replies to.

subjectState.description: What moderation has done with it: `visible`, `held` or `removed`.

text.description: What was said, as text. Empty for an account.

openCount.description: Open items, for the menu badge.

blockIndex.description: Index of the paragraph in the snapshot scene.

kind.description: Sending the kind already there clears it, the way a repeated vote does.

percent.description: Furthest point reached, as a percentage of the published scenes.

furthestIndex.description:
The furthest they ever reached, which is the interesting one: a reader
who gave up in chapter three and later skimmed the ending has still
stopped in chapter three.

codes.description: Shown once. Each gets someone in once if the authenticator is lost.

acceptTerms.description: Agreement to the terms in force (`GET /api/terms`). Required.

ids.description:
The entries of that kind, in their new order. Any left out keep their
order among themselves, after the ones listed.

kind.description: The kind being arranged: entries are ordered within their kind.

ids.description: Every queued prompt's id, in the new order.
Complete ordered list of ids; anything missing keeps its current slot.

commentBody.description: What was said, so the author can judge without going to find it.

support.description: Present for a self-harm report: where to find help.

oneOf.description: The scene as it stands after applying it, when one was applied.

outline.description: The work's outline, as it now stands.

safetyVersion.description: The snapshot taken of the working copy before it was replaced.

scenesRemoved.description:
Scenes that existed only in the working copy and were removed. They are
in `safetyVersion`, which is the point of taking it.

confirmName.description:
For a restriction that ends in deletion: the account's display name,
typed to confirm.

days.description:
3, 7 or 30. Absent: permanent. Ignored for a site-wide read-only
restriction, which is always the 30 days before deletion.

reasonCode.description: A section of the community guidelines.

reasonText.description: The message the writer is shown.

linkedItems.description: JSON array of the queue items that prompted it.

reasonCode.description: A section of the community guidelines.

reasonText.description: The message the writer is shown.

ReviewHistoryItem.description: One publication someone reviewed, as their profile shows it.

resolved.description: Notes the author marked resolved — that they acted on it.

commentId.description:
The note it came from, or `None` for one the author typed themselves —
or one whose comment has since been deleted. The task is the author's
either way.

quote.description: The passage it was written against, when it was.

blocks.description:
Paragraph-aligned diff against the scene as it stands now — what
restoring this revision would change.

baseHash.description:
The hash the edit was made on top of; a save against something newer
is refused with 409, as scene saves are.

localDay.description: The writer's own date, for their daily goal.

excluded.description:
Kept in the outline but not part of the book: not exported, not in a
version, not in the book's word count. New scenes are part of it, and
so is one a client cached before this existed: absent means `false`.

storyDate.description: Free text: fiction rarely runs on the Gregorian calendar.

targetWords.description: A target for this scene, for writers who plan at that level.

blocks.description: Paragraph by paragraph, for a modified scene.

snippet.description:
A few words around the match; matched words sit between U+0002 and
U+0003.

Which chapters and scenes go in.

A flat object rather than a tagged union, so every client can model it
without one: `kind` says whether the ids count.

chapterIds.description: A chapter id selects the chapter and every scene in it.

sceneIds.description:
A scene id on its own selects just that scene (under its chapter's
title).

Sense.description: One meaning of the word, and the words for it.

gloss.description: What this sense means, briefly, to tell it from the others.

related.description: Near it: similar words, and more particular ones ("walk" → "march").

userAgent.description: What the device said it was, for telling sessions apart in a list.

current.description: The session this request came from.

url.description: The whole link, to send to someone.

to.description: What it is being measured against.

SketchField.description: One named part of a sketch.

key.description: Stable within the entry; a field the writer added gets one too.

prompt.description:
The question the field asks, from its template. Absent on the writer's
own fields.

atBlock.description:
Index of the first top-level block that belongs to the *new* scene.
Blocks, not characters: the cut is between paragraphs, which is how a
writer thinks about "this should have been two scenes".

baseHash.description:
The `contentHash` the split was decided against. Required, unlike on an
ordinary save: splitting rewrites prose in two places, and doing that to
a document someone else has edited would be much worse than refusing.

title.description: Title for the new scene. Defaults to the original's, with a suffix.

first.description: The original scene, now holding only the blocks before the cut.

second.description: The new scene, holding the rest.

signOut.description: Also sign out every device now.

StaleChange.description: Why a change could not be applied, for a client that has to explain it.

Standing.description:
How useful a reviewer's feedback has turned out to be.

Derived on read rather than kept in a column: it is a function of rows that
already exist, and a stored copy would only be a second thing to get wrong.

resolved.description: Notes a work's author marked resolved — them saying they acted on it.

votes.description: Net votes across everything this reviewer has written.

writePath.description: The last minute and the last fifteen.

StyleOptions.description:
Typography. A preset plus overrides on top of it; `None` means the preset's
own value. The manuscript preset ignores every override: fixing them is the
point of the format.

sceneBreak.description: `⁂`, `* * *`, `#`, an empty string for a blank line, or custom text.

Summary.description: What is going out, in numbers.

cached.description: True when this is an earlier answer for the same text, not a new call.

oneOf.description: The note it came from, if it came from one and that note still stands.

prompt.description: The question the field is asking.

body.description: Prefilled prose, if the template wants to seed the scene with a prompt.

appliesTo.description: Where it applies. Never private writing.

surface.description: A surface, to see what would happen there. Default `comment`.

base.description:
The form it was found under: "walked" is found as "walk". When the word
is both a word and a form of another ("running"), this is the other,
and its senses come first.

blankParagraphSplits.description: Whether a blank paragraph separated scenes, from the writer's setting.

title.description: A title from the prompt, for the dialog to offer.
Unset, the title the preview offered.

baseHash.description:
The scene's `contentHash` when the proposal was written. `None` on rows
predating this column; those always re-anchor by their quotation.

secret.description: The key to type into an authenticator by hand.

url.description: The same key as an `otpauth://` link, for a QR code or a tap.

count.description: Unread items, plus one for an unread summary.

from.description: Where the passage is now, after the draft moved it.

quote.description: The passage as it reads now, when the writer has edited it.

role.description:
`chapter`, `front` (preface, foreword), `back` (acknowledgments,
afterword, appendix) or `part` (a divider that opens a run of
chapters). Front and back matter and parts are not numbered as
chapters. A chapter made a part is given an empty scene if it has none:
its part page, which keeps it in a version even with nothing on it.

chapterIds.description:
Narrow them to exactly these chapters. An empty list leaves them
nowhere to write, which is not the same as everywhere.

wholeWork.description: `true` hands them the whole work again.

state.description: `open` or `resolved`; only the author of the work may resolve.

fields.description: The whole sketch, in order. Replaces what was there.

dailyWordGoal.description: `null` clears the target; leaving it out leaves it alone.

UpdateMetadataRequest.description:
Each field is sent only when it changes; an empty string (or list) clears
it, which is what a writer emptying the field in the UI means.

identifier.description: An ISBN or any other identifier. Optional; never required.

aboutAuthor.description:
A paragraph about the writer, offered as back matter in any book's
export. An empty string clears it.

unpin.description: Take it off its day and put it at the end of the queue.

chapterId.description: Move the scene into a different chapter of the same work.

excluded.description:
Leave the scene out of the book (`true`) or put it back: an excluded
scene is not exported, not in a version, and not in the word count.

storyDate.description: Free text: fiction rarely runs on the Gregorian calendar.

targetWords.description:
A word target for this scene. Omit to leave it alone; send `null` to
clear it. The nesting is what distinguishes those two — see
`present_or_absent`.

doubleEnterSplitsScenes.description:
A blank paragraph (double Enter) is a scene break, while writing a book
and when turning text into a project.

oneOf.description: How the app looks, on every device the writer signs in on.

notes.description: What this snapshot was for. Blank clears it.

penName.description:
Front matter. Each is sent only when it changes; an empty string clears
one, which is what a writer emptying the field in the UI means.

targetDate.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` to reach it by. An empty string clears it.

targetWords.description: How long the book is meant to be. `0` clears it.

aboutAuthor.description: A paragraph about the writer, reusable as back matter in any book.

assistantAllowedAt.description:
When they agreed that text they hand the writing assistant may be sent
to the model provider. Separate from summaries: a different use.

dailyWordGoal.description: The writer's daily target in words, when they have set one.

doubleEnterSplitsScenes.description:
A blank paragraph (double Enter) is a scene break: in the web book
editor it moves on to the next scene, and turning text into a project
splits there as well as at a `--` line.

emailVerifiedAt.description:
When the address was proved. Invitations addressed to it reach this
account only once it has been.

isAdmin.description:
A site administrator: curates the daily prompts. Set from the command
line only; no request body can change it.

isModerator.description:

legalName.description:
Contact details for a submission's first page. Kept on the writer rather
than the work, since they are the same for every submission.

summariesAllowedAt.description:
When they agreed that text they ask to summarise may be sent to the
model provider. Unset, no summary is ever asked for on their behalf.

termsVersion.description: The version of the terms they last agreed to.

theme.description: How the app looks for them, on every device.

totpEnabledAt.description: When two-factor sign-in was turned on.

weeklyWordGoal.description: The writer's weekly target in words, when they have set one.

actions.description: What the viewer may do here, so the page shows only those buttons.

ladder.description: The suggested next step on the escalation ladder.

statusEnds.description: When the restriction behind the status ends. Absent when permanent.

scope.description: `work`, `chapter` or `scene` — how much of the book this froze.

page.description: Which chapter of `toc` this page holds, from zero.

toc.description:
Every chapter on offer, in order, when this is one page of them — so a
reader can move between pages and count progress along the whole book.

tags.description: Free-form labels, lowercased so `Submitted` and `submitted` are one tag.

chapterRole.description: The chapter's role when the snapshot was taken.

pinned.description: Whether this is the work's pinned snapshot.

tags.description:
Tags, but not the manifest: a list of fifty snapshots has no use for
fifty manifests.

value.description: `1` upvote, `-1` downvote, `0` clears the caller's vote.

dbWritesPerSecond.description: Database calls made while serving them.

lockWaitMs.description: Sampled: how long the write lock took to get, every few seconds.

oneOf.description:
What to browse it under. Unset is allowed: plenty of writers do not
know yet.

penName.description: The name on the byline, when it is not the writer's own.

pinnedVersionId.description:
The snapshot the writer wants to find without looking — what they last
sent out.

shortTitle.description: Short form for a running header; a long title wraps and ruins it.

targetDate.description: The day they mean to get there by, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

targetWords.description: How long the book is meant to be, when the writer has said.

chapterIds.description:
The chapters they may change, when they were handed only some. Absent
means the whole work. Reading is never narrowed.

creator.description: Whether they started the work — the one thing an added owner is not.

subject.description: The title as it was at the time.

times.description: How many acts this line stands for.

WritingPlace.description:
